title: Introduce warmup tracker and eviction stabilizer for KV cache
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: high churn on tenant-heavy workloads causes oscillatory eviction behavior and expensive spillovers during sudden load ramps. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a lightweight warmup tracker that detects tenant/model hot windows and pre-allocates 'warm' reservation credits to reduce cold eviction churn during scale-ups; (2) an eviction stabilizer that smooths eviction rate via a sliding-window occupancy witness and a hysteresis-backed preemptive-spill threshold to avoid aggressive cascade spill events. Goals: reduce token-serving latency spikes during tenant warmups, lower total bytes spilled to disk, and make eviction behavior less sensitive to micro-bursty scheduling decisions. Summary of changes: - new runtime component: kv/warmup_tracker.go (heuristics-based warm windows and per-tenant warm credits) - eviction stabilizer: kv/eviction_stabilizer.go (occupancy witness, EWMA of eviction pressure, hysteresis gates) - scheduler integration: runtime/scheduler/evict_hint.go (avoid eviction passes while continuous-batcher is actively processing tenant prefixes) - kernel hinting: runtime/kernels/hint_eviction.cu (small perf hints to reduce allocation stalls when eviction is withheld) - config knobs/feature flag: config/kv_warmup.yaml and feature gate warmup_eviction_stabilizer - telemetry: metrics and traces (metrics/kv_warmup.md) - unit and integration tests plus a focused perf benchmark harness under bench/kv_warmup_bench.go Compatibility: feature gated off by default; conservative defaults chosen after local perf tuning. Checklist: - [x] Add warmup tracker algorithm and tests - [x] Integrate stabilizer with eviction path and scheduler - [x] Add metrics and dashboards guidance - [x] Add config knobs and feature gate - [x] Run cluster-level soak and perf bench (results summarized below) Bench/soak summary: in a 3-node dedicated pool with mixed tenant traffic (10K tenants synthetic, 30% heavy, 10% bursty), end-to-end tail P95 token latency during 10s warm ramps improved by 22% and bytes spilled decreased by 37% compared to baseline. Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout to staging for a week, then to dedicated pools behind canary routing. Known limitations: heuristics may under-allocate warm credits for extremely short-lived bursts (<100ms) — see follow-up ENG-4870 for adaptive sampling improvements. Related work: builds on prior eviction-rate-shapers (ENG-4322) and the preemptive-spill experiments (ENG-3886).

review_conversation: Jordan Li: Overall this looks promising. Two main asks: add a unit test that simulates back-to-back ramps and validate no oscillation, and add more comments around the warm credit decay policy.
Aisha Kapoor: Added a new test 'TestWarmupPreventsOscillation' and expanded comments in warmup_tracker.go; warm credits decay via exponential backoff with configurable half-life (default 60s).
Marina Ortega: Can we avoid holding the eviction mutex while computing the occupancy witness? Suggest sampling a snapshot and doing work off the hot path.
Aisha Kapoor: Refactored stabilizer to sample atomic counters under short lock then compute EWMA off-path; updated tests to assert no lock amplification.
Devon Park: Perf harness results? The CUDA hint file is sensitive; did you measure any regressions on fast-path allocations?
Aisha Kapoor: Bench results included in PR description; microbench showed <1% median allocation overhead and 12% reduced stall frequency during warm ramps. Also added a CI perf job to the PR runs.
Jordan Li: Approving after small nits addressed. Marina and Devon approved as well.
release_notes: Introduce optional KV warmup tracker and eviction stabilizer to reduce eviction-induced spill and tail latency during tenant warmups. Feature gated off by default.
notes_for_ops: Feature off by default. To enable: flip feature gate 'warmup_eviction_stabilizer' in config/kv_warmup.yaml and monitor metrics 'kv.warmup.credits' and 'kv.eviction.stabilizer.pressure_ewma'. Recommended to rollout to a small canary fleet then monitor spill bytes and P95 token latency.
